about: Known alerts of the OWASP ZAP scan (dev/tests/zap.js): false positives and accepted findings. id = ZAP plugin id (or alertRef), url / param: optional regexes an instance must match (the url is the full address), reason: why it is accepted. An alert instance that matches no entry counts as unknown – Medium / High fail the suite. Keep entries as narrow as the reason allows.

known.reason: form pages: nuBuilder Forte's form code runs there – nuOnLoad, object events and nuBuilder's eval() of code strings need script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval', objects and the designer set style attributes (style-src 'unsafe-inline'), image objects may show pictures of other sites (img-src https:). nuBuilder Next's own pages keep the strict policy (self only), see Help → Security

code editors and TinyMCE: the procedure page evaluates nuOnProcedureRun() of its JavaScript tab as nuBuilder Forte does ('unsafe-eval'), TinyMCE sets inline styles ('unsafe-inline' for styles only); scripts stay 'self'
sign-in page with a custom HTML from nuconfig.php ($nuWelcomeBodyInnerHTML): inline style attributes of that HTML are allowed, scripts are not
folder addresses answered by PHP's built-in test server with its own 404 page – Apache and nginx serve their own error pages; no page of nuBuilder Next
static files on PHP's built-in test server, which adds no headers; on Apache the root .htaccess sets X-Content-Type-Options for every file, nginx with the add_header rule of the Security check
static files on PHP's built-in test server (expose_php); nuBuilder Next's own answers remove the X-Powered-By header
the documentation mentions error texts and driver names (ODBC Driver, SQLSTATE …) – ZAP takes them for an error message of the page
the documentation shows addresses such as 127.0.0.1 and 192.168.x.x as examples
numbers that look like Unix timestamps: version stamps, ids and dates in lists – no secret
the user name as a list filter in the address (?user=…) – a filter of the admin lists, not a credential
